Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline can identify every affected member and the card charged, so a claims process is unnecessary. We propose $35 million for automatic payments to the class, plus $7 million in court-approved fees and expenses. Any fee reduction would increase class relief. We are open to a counterproposal that preserves meaningful automatic payments.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that identified members should receive automatic payments, without a claims process. Your proposal exceeds Brightline’s settlement authority. We offer a $28 million class fund plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses. We would not seek a provision returning any fee reduction to Brightline; instead, that amount would increase class relief. We welcome your response.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can reduce our proposed fee request to $6 million, but seek a $32 million class fund. That would deliver $80 per identified member before any additional amount from a fee reduction, without requiring claims.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement on fees and agree that automatic payments are appropriate. To narrow the remaining gap, Brightline offers a $30 million class fund plus $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees added to class relief. We would not request a claims process or a fee reversion.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $30 million class fund distributed automatically, plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with any unawarded fees added to class relief. We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to avoid both a claims process and fee reversion.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with substantial automatic class relief, reflecting the $64 million in disputed charges and litigation risk. Keep fees separate and reasonable, with any reduction benefiting the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

Their proposal totals $42 million, above Brightline’s $40 million authorization. Counter at $34 million total, preserving automatic payments and directing any fee reduction to the class. This leaves room to negotiate while offering substantial relief.

The defense offer preserves automatic payments and directs any unawarded fees to the class, but there is room to negotiate the class fund upward. Keep the fee request at $6 million rather than trading class recovery for fees.

The $38 million proposal is within authority and uses court-friendly terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Counter at $36 million while preserving automatic payments and fee reductions for the class.

The $30 million automatic class fund exceeds the $27.5 million expected trial recovery before accounting for certification risk, delay, and costs. The $6 million fee remains subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. This is a strong, defensible resolution.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: On behalf of the proposed class, we negotiated a $30 million class fund for automatic payments to approximately 400,000 identifiable members—about $75 per member—plus up to $6 million in court-approved attorneys’ fees and expenses paid separately by Brightline. We initially proposed a $35 million class fund and $7 million in fees. Brightline countered with $28 million and $6 million; we then proposed $32 million and $6 million. Brightline offered $30 million and $6 million, which we accepted. Throughout the negotiations, both sides agreed that members should not have to file claims. The settlement contains no clear-sailing provision, and any fees the court declines to award will increase class relief rather than return to Brightline. Fees were discussed from the first round, not only after class relief was agreed. In my judgment, the settlement is fair to the class: it provides substantial, automatic recovery now despite unresolved certification risk and the uncertainty and delay of litigation. It remains subject to the court’s independent review, including review of the fee request.
